content.summary: Four focused scope tests found no contradiction to the stated theorem imports. Explicit countermodels invalidate broader readings that the manuscript correctly excludes. Assignment hashes and inspected evidence hashes matched. This is a bounded source-and-scope review, not complete proof validation.

findings.statement: The empty-core convention, rho<=7 restriction in R16, strict Jin inequality and cap18 guard are essential. The inspected manuscript preserves each rather than using the corresponding broader claim.
findings.disposition: No revision is required from these tests. The countermodels below target omitted-hypothesis readings, not the manuscript's actual theorem. No solver or full replay was run.

revisions.action: Retested the exact scope of the principal graph and classification imports.
revisions.result: The imported-theorem and local-replay limitations remain accurate; this round does not upgrade their assurance.

revisions.action: Reopened the pinned prior comparison record and rechecked its numerical convention.
revisions.result: The one-unit comparison remains supported; no exhaustive priority conclusion is inferred.

revisions.action: Used the source map to test omitted-hypothesis counterreadings and dependency order.
revisions.result: The tested map entries retain their necessary guards. No earlier required revision is outstanding for this reviewer.

checks.scope: Maximum-size convention, forcing threshold and empty cores
checks.method: Reopened aiXiv v1 metadata, compared manuscript sections 1-2, and constructed 68 disjoint four-sets {4i,...,4i+3} for 0<=i<68 with standard-library pair checks.
checks.observation: The prior source excludes size69 and reports maximum<=68, while the present statement excludes size68 and reports maximum<=67. The constructed disjoint family has no nonempty-core sunflower but has empty-core sunflowers, showing why omitting empty cores would invalidate the intended claim. Both sources explicitly include them. [Prior v1 record](https://aixiv.online/abs/2610.01292).

checks.scope: R16 is not a classification of every size16 SF3 family
checks.method: Read pinned paper/main.tex lines443-454 and tested all triples of members in the literal family P10 union a disjoint translate by6 of its first six displayed blocks.
checks.observation: The test family has16 members,12 support points, no three-sunflower and rho=10, so it is not the ten-point R16 model. It refutes an unguarded size16 classification but lies outside the source's rho<=7 domain. Manuscript section3 and the source map retain that restriction.

checks.scope: Jin strictness and the extra argument for occupied A3 fibres
checks.method: Read Nikiforov v1 PDF page2, Theorem A and its tightness paragraph; read direct-jin; checked integer threshold margins and every coefficient of the eight cyclic inversion identities.
checks.observation: The actual margins are25*11-4*68=3 and24*20-7*68=4. The source's A4 boundary has equality at k=3 and does not support weakening > to >=. All eight identities b_i+b_(i+3)+b_(i+5)-sum(a)=a_i checked exactly. The add-on uses b_i<=27 and total deficit12 to obtain a_i>=1 before b_i>=25; surjectivity is not imported from Jin. [Theorem A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.2070v1).

checks.scope: Universal versus cap18-guarded imports and hereditary restriction
checks.method: Compared manuscript sections3-4 with GLOBAL67-dependency-roadmap.md sections1-2, PRIOR_DELTA18_UNLOCK.md and pinned paper/main.tex lines968-970 and1027-1029.
checks.observation: Crowding and R61 require mu>=41 and Delta<=18, with a complete R16 link additionally required for R61. The recorded chain activates this package after degree20 and19 exclusions; its unrestricted small-rank inputs are separately identified. Reduction to68 uses hereditary sunflower-freeness, recomputes mu, and explicitly forbids inheriting minimum positive degree after arbitrary deletion. No misuse of those source scopes was found in this composition check.

provenance.tool: collaboration.followup_task; specialist-authored public JSON artifact and observed final response
